findings.text: non-blocking: the narrowed catch at line 205 handles only CrewError, but read_pointer (reckon/crew/runs.py:819-857) can raise a plain OSError from path.stat() or path.read_text() (EACCES, EIO on the shared home). Such an error now escapes _unreconciled_runs_remedy and classify_pointer, so one unreadable pointer aborts the whole classification loop in reckon/crew/obligations.py:547 or reckon/crew/query.py; before this branch touched the filesystem it could not. An OSError should keep the duty the way an unparseable pointer does.

non-blocking: `assert refusal["next_command"] == action` compares the code's output against the same `action` string the test passed into UnreconciledRuns in the line above, so it holds whenever the reader echoes its input and cannot detect a regression in run selection; the same echo shape is at line 136. The discriminating guards for this change are the pointer-gone case at line 145, the two-run case at line 206 and _assert_no_redispatch at line 110.
